newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Arsenic pollution threatens 15 mln Bangladeshis.
newsitem.headline: Arsenic pollution threatens 15 mln Bangladeshis.

text.p: Arsenic contamination of sub-soil water threatened 15 million people in northern and southwestern Bangladesh, the Independent newspaper said on Thursday, quoting health officials.

At least three people died of prolonged illness recently that local doctors determined was from arsenic contamination in a remote village of Bengari in southwestern Chuadanga district bordering India's West Bengal state, the newspaper said.

Nearly 75 percent of the inhabitants at Bengari village were suffering from diseases caused by prolonged intake of arsenic contaminated water, it said quoting a survey by a group of non-government organisations (NGOs).
The survey found patients had developed severe rashes mainly on palms and foot, and were suffering from chronic intestinal complications.
Health officials have sealed off six tubewells in the village found pumping water with high levels of arsenic content.

Doctors at Chuadanga hospital said they had sought urgent help from the Health Department in Dhaka to deal with the growing arsenic contamination, which Bangladesh's Health Minister Salahuddin Yusuf recently called a "public health crisis."
A government-sponsored committee with doctors and scientists was investigating the extent of arsenic pollution and its causes, health officials in Dhaka said.
They said country's hospitals had so far treated more than 1,000 cases of arsenic poisoning.
Authorities in recent months have sealed off hundreds of tubewells in affected areas and asked people to drink surface water.

The Dhaka office of the World Health Organisation on Tuesday expressed concern at the growing problem of arsenic contamination and advised the government to draw up "carefully planned actions" to deal with the health hazard.
